newsitem.title: UK: Orange up, Vodafone off on OFTEL news.
newsitem.headline: Orange up, Vodafone off on OFTEL news.

text.p: Orange Plc shares rose and Vodafone Plc shares fell after telecoms watchdog OFTEL said it was relaxing some curbs on mobile phone operators, telecommunications analysts said.
Orange put on 3-1/2p to 218p, Vodafone shed 3-1/2p to 267-1/2p and Securicor Group Plc, which owns 40 percent of Cellnet, was unchanged at 285p.
Cable and Wireless Plc, which owns part of One2One, eased 1/2p to 484-1/2p.
British Telecommunications Plc, which owns 60 percent of Cellnet, still benefitting from its shareholders approving the merger with MCI, rose 3-12p to 444p.

"OFTEL saying that the industry no longer needs service providers looks mildly favourable for all of them although Orange and One2One already own their own service providers," said Credit Lyonnais Laing telecoms analyst Steve Scruton.

"But on the negative side most important is what OFTEL has said about prices being aligned with costs. This is especially negative for Vodafone and Cellnet whose prices are higher and costs lower - the interconnect fee is higher," he said.
Scruton said comments on number portability and more consumer friendly contracts were also mildly negative for all mobile phone companies.
OFTEL said the changes would be brought in for Orange and One2One in about six months and later for the larger operators, Vodafone and Cellnet.
